Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — PulseHealth is excited to move forward. Per our conversation, the implementation team needs a concise model + context spec and token roadmap that we can use internally (engineering + procurement). Key asks from our side:

- A shortlist of 2–3 model tiers (recommended model variants) with suggested max context lengths.
- Expected tokens per session and total daily token volume for the first 90 days (we provided a small sample of typical messages).
- Guidance on fallback models and what changes in latency/cost to expect.
- Anything you need from our side to finalize the plan.

I attached a small CSV with 50 anonymized message samples and a simple session mapping (pulse_token_sample.csv). We expect an initial active user base of ~7k weekly active users; typical support session length is 8–12 messages. Peak concurrency estimate: 120 concurrent sessions.

Can your team provide a short roadmap and a recommended canary ramp plan? Procurement would like a draft by end of next week to begin the internal review.

Appreciate it —
Samir

Hi Monica — quick answers below (sorry for the delay).

1) Yes — retrieval will be used in ~40% of sessions. Typical document fetch is 2–3 KB, usually 1–2 docs per retrieval.
2) For triage chat we'd like P95 < 500ms. For clinical summary generation we can tolerate up to ~1.2s if it improves quality.
3) Priority mapping: triage chat (latency-sensitive), patient-facing conversational replies (balance), clinician summary (quality-first).

I've also shared our product spec with the engineering team (link: https://drive.google.com/pulse/product-spec) — see section 3 for session types.

Subject: Proposed model shortlist, context bands, and 90-day token roadmap (PulseHealth)

Team — consolidating our recommendations based on the samples and the product spec. This is intended to be a pragmatic plan you can hand to procurement and eng for canary planning. Actionable items are at the bottom.

Executive summary
- Recommended shortlist: 1) Redwood-Medium-8k (default, good latency/quality tradeoff) 2) Redwood-High-16k (for clinician summaries) 3) Redwood-Lite-4k (fallback for burst / cost control).
- Retrieval: enable prefix caching + doc-attached prompts; budget additional ~30–40 tokens per retrieval (2–3 KB doc).
- Expected tokens/session (median / 95th): triage chat 600 / 1,800; patient conv 900 / 2,400; clinician summary 2,800 / 6,500.
- 90-day token roadmap (conservative): day-0 daily tokens = 1.1M; week-4 = 3.5M; week-12 = 6.2M (based on 7k WAU ramp to 25k).

Model guidance (shortlist)
1) Redwood-Medium-8k
- Use case: triage chat & patient conv (default).
- Context: 8k tokens to allow full session + 1 doc retrieval.
- Expected latency: P95 ~350–450ms on Dedicated capacity with small-batch concurrency.
- Cost: baseline (reference) — see attached spreadsheet for per-1M token costs.

2) Redwood-High-16k
- Use case: clinician summaries & long-context generation.
- Context: 16k tokens to include multiple docs + session history.
- Expected latency: P95 ~650–900ms (depends on doc retrieval policy).
- Cost: ~2.3x Redwood-Medium for same token count due to larger kernels.

3) Redwood-Lite-4k (fallback)
- Use case: burst handling, low-cost QA or unattended batch jobs.
- Context: 4k tokens, quantized; suitable when cost-sensitive.
- Expected latency: P95 ~300–500ms; lower quality on long summaries.

Routing & fallbacks
- Policy: default route to Redwood-Medium-8k. For clinician-summary flows, route to Redwood-High-16k. On overload, autoscale or fallback to Redwood-Lite-4k with grace degradation notice in responses.
- Retries: implement single automatic retry to same-tier, then fallback to Lite if latency budget exceeded.

90-day operational ramp (high-level)
- Canary week (week 0): 1% traffic to Redwood-Medium-8k, baseline monitoring for latency, token burn, and quality on a small eval set.
- Week 1–4: ramp to 10% → 30% → 60% with gates at token burn and quality drift.
- Week 5–12: full rollout to production lanes; keep Redwood-Lite-4k available for overflow.

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Redwood: provide per-1M token cost table + initial billing estimate for weeks 0/4/12 (Vivek) — ETA 2026-09-15.
- PulseHealth: confirm traffic ramp targets and any regulatory data-locality needs (Samir) — ETA 2026-09-14.
- Redwood: prepare canary eval prompt set (Grace) and short integration checklist (Jordan) — ETA 2026-09-16.

Attachments: redwood_model_shortlist.xlsx (pricing + perf assumptions included).

Let me know if you'd like a quick call Tuesday to walk through the cost table and fallbacks.

Thanks —
Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
